svg.title: Model routing picks a model before running the query; cascading runs a cheap model first and escalates only when it fails an acceptance test.
svg.desc: Routing uses a classifier or LLM judge to send each query to one model based on predicted complexity, deciding once before execution. Cascading is the sequential variant: a query starts with a cheaper model and escalates to a larger one only when a scoring function rejects the cheap model's answer. RouteLLM reports an 85% cost reduction while retaining 95% of GPT-4 quality on its MT-Bench setup; FrugalGPT reports up to 98% lower cost in its evaluated model pool.

text.font-family: Space Grotesk, IBM Plex Sans, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif

svg.text: Routing decides once; cascading escalates on failure

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif

svg.text: Both send eligible traffic to a cheaper model — they differ in when that decision happens.
